# Candidate coverage map for SANY

Primary scope `cli-noexp` (the SANY command line, Explorer cut, XMLExporter excluded): **3892 of 5010 handwritten branches are candidates under RTA (3986 under CHA); specs alone hit 79.3% of them, the union 81.3%.** Generated code: 6509 of 6564 candidates, specs 80.9%, union 81.0%. For comparison, against all 5010 handwritten branches the union is 74.9%.

**What this is.** Static call-graph reachability over the pinned class files: an upper bound on what can run. A branch in this map has not been ruled out; nothing here claims it can be taken, and whether it can is undecidable in general. A branch outside the map cannot run from these entry points, given the assumptions under "Limits". No model, no network, no clock: the same input gives the same bytes.

**Rerun, from the repository root:** `go run ./cmd/staticreach -jdk $JAVA_HOME`, after `scripts/setup reference` and `scripts/maintainer/unpack-classes`.

It reads the JaCoCo reports committed in `data/staticreach`, starts no JVM and runs no SANY code, writes this report plus `candidate-map.tsv` and `candidate-map-branches.tsv` under `.work/staticreach`, then runs the soundness check and exits 1 on anything unexplained. The check here covers 2 report rows, both of the plain command; the measurement it was first run on covered 14, with the measuring wrapper and upstream's test classes on the path, neither of which is committed here. Scopes, cuts and run-to-scope assignments are in `cmd/staticreach/scopes.conf`; `-scopes` reads another file.

Definitions. CHA dispatches a virtual call on an application type to every concrete subtype. RTA dispatches only to classes instantiated in reachable code. JDK callbacks count under both, and only for classes instantiated in reachable code: an unrestricted `Object.toString` would otherwise pull in all 2019 classes and make the Explorer cut meaningless. RTA+const adds the one intra-method refinement below.

## The exporter is secondary

`XMLExporter` is not part of parsing a spec, so the primary scope leaves it out. It stays as the `cli+xml` rows because the L3 differential oracle uses it as a test harness tool, which is why its runs are in the coverage reports. Adding it grows the handwritten denominator from 3892 to 4264 under RTA, and the specs' hits inside the scope from 3085 to 3316.

Hits in the primary scope that came only from exporter runs: **at most 17 of 3085 handwritten and 31 of 5266 generated (RTA)**. That is an upper bound, method by method: specs minus the plain command-line passes (`cli-ABC`, `cli-D`, `cli-E`). The exec files merge the probe JVM and the exporter JVM per case and the per-JVM files are gone, so an exporter hit cannot be told from a `SanyProbe` hit. `cli-D` and `cli-E` were last run before tiers D and E stopped growing, so cases kept since then count here too. Hits the other way, CLI ahead of specs: 0.

## Guard shapes: a separate number

**These are shapes, not proof.** `if (x != null)` can be real logic. Guard numbers are a reading aid: they never alter the map, the scopes or the soundness check, and the tables above do not use them.

Attribution is per branch instruction and per arm. JaCoCo's public API stops at per-line counts, so `cmd/staticreach/java/.../BranchProbes.java` runs JaCoCo's own probe flow and filters and reads each instruction's covered arms before they are summed. The tool fails if those arms do not add up to JaCoCo's own per-method counters in the XML. So `candidate-map-branches.tsv` names the missed arm of every branch.

Each cell is raw / excluding excludable missed arms on instructions that ran (another arm hit) / excluding also those on instructions that never ran. Under RTA, not refined. Only the denominator moves.

Shapes, first match wins:

- `assert`: `$assertionsDisabled` just before the branch, or an arm that builds an `AssertionError` and throws. Only the throwing arm is excludable. JaCoCo already filters the `$assertionsDisabled` guard itself.
- `scaffold-class` (generated): any branch in `ParseException`, `SimpleCharStream`, `Token`, `TokenMgrError`, `TLAplusParserConstants`.
- `jj_ntk-cache` (generated): `(jj_ntk==-1)?jj_ntk():jj_ntk`, seen as `getfield jj_ntk; iconst_m1; if_icmp`.
- `jj_scan_token` (generated): the branch straight after a call to it.
- `jj_3R` (generated): any other branch in a `jj_3R_*` or `jj_3_*` lookahead method.
- `null`: `ifnull`, `ifnonnull`. Either missed arm is excludable.
- `instanceof`: `instanceof` then a branch. Either missed arm is excludable.
- `throw-arm`: one arm reaches `athrow` with no other branch on the way. Only that arm is excludable: if the other arm is the missed one, the code has only ever thrown, which is not a guard left alone.
- `switch-default`: a switch's default arm. Only the default is excludable.

### The prototype's figures

Prototype (`guards.py`): handwritten specs 73.2% / 75.6% / 81.3%, union 80.6% / 83.8% / 87.0%; generated specs 80.9% to 81.3%. These are corrected, for two reasons:

1. **Scope.** The prototype's denominator was 4,227: it matched methods and JDK callbacks by bare name, and cut the Explorer by package prefix only. Exact signatures and the real edge cut give 3892 in the primary scope, so the raw figures move before any guard is counted.
2. **Attribution.** The prototype classified lines and removed every missed outcome on a guard line. Arms are finer: the non-throwing arm of a throw guard stays. Its per-line rule, rerun on this tool's scopes, gives:

| scope | specs | union |
|---|---|---|
| `cli-noexp`, handwritten, per line | 79.2 / 82.3 / 85.8 | 81.3 / 84.3 / 87.6 |
| `cli`, handwritten, per line | 72.3 / 74.8 / 81.3 | 77.0 / 80.2 / 84.6 |

On `cli` the per-line rule lands within a point of the prototype for specs; its union figures remain 2 to 4 points higher. That gap was not reconciled method by method.

Generated code moves once the generated shapes count: specs 80.9% to 87.6%, not 81.3%. The prototype had no `jj_*` classes, so it saw only null checks there.

## Cutting the Explorer

Bytecode scan of all 2019 classes: `new tla2sany/explorer/Explorer` occurs 1 time(s): `tla2sany/drivers/SANY.SANYmain0`, line 760. That is `drivers/SANY.java`'s `if (doDebugging)` block, entered only with `-d` or `-D`. The cut removes the body, lines 760-764, and the guard's true outcome; the guard itself on line 758 stays, because it runs. No Java source changes.

Other references into `tla2sany/explorer/` from outside the package, by target: `Explorer.<init>` 1, `Explorer.main` 1, `ExplorerVisitor.<init>` 4, `ExplorerVisitor.NoopVisitor` 1, `ExplorerVisitor.get` 1, `ExplorerVisitor.postVisit` 27, `ExplorerVisitor.preVisit` 27, `new Explorer` 1. Apart from the `Explorer` sites at lines 760 and 762, all of them use `ExplorerVisitor`, a plain visitor type, which can stay reachable without any `Explorer`.

Do the methods semantic nodes implement for `ExploreNode` drop out once `Explorer` is gone? Methods (branches):

| methods | with Explorer, RTA | Explorer cut, RTA | with Explorer, CHA | Explorer cut, CHA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `walkGraph`, `walkGaph` | 29 (160) | 0 (0) | 29 (160) | 0 (0) |
| `toString(int, Errors)` | 30 (234) | 27 (224) | 30 (234) | 27 (224) |
| `levelDataToString` | 11 (26) | 0 (0) | 11 (26) | 0 (0) |

`walkGraph`, `walkGaph` and `levelDataToString` drop out. **Depth-taking `toString` does not.** Its route is `SymbolTable.toString()`, which calls `Context.getContextEntryStringVector`: `SymbolTable` is instantiated, so its `toString()` counts as a JDK callback. The bytecode has 0 direct calls or string concatenations on that type, so only the assumption that the JDK may stringify any instantiated object keeps it. No report ran it. In `cli-noexp` this is a what-if, not applied: without that one method's calls 27 of these `toString` methods (224 branches) drop and 0 (0 branches) stay, and the whole scope falls by 319 branches. Proving that no `SymbolTable` reaches a JDK call needs points-to analysis, so the raw scopes keep them. Chris chose to cut it by hand in `port`, as the named entry `symboltable-tostring` in `scopes.conf`, which he can veto.

The cut removes 374 branches under RTA in all, 196 of them in those explore methods. Largest classes (methods, branches): `Explorer` 11, 106; `OpApplNode` 1, 40; `OpDefNode` 3, 38; `DotExplorerVisitor` 8, 24; `SyntaxTreeNode` 1, 22; `ModuleNode` 3, 14; `ExternalModuleTable` 6, 12; `APSubstInNode` 1, 10; `SubstInNode` 1, 10; `Context` 4, 8; `ExternalModuleTable$ExternalModuleTableEntry` 4, 8; `DotExplorerVisitor$NoopTable` 2, 6;

## Intra-method refinement

One rule, in `refine.go`: a branch on a field or a static method whose value the closed world fixes is folded, and code only that branch reaches is dead. A field qualifies when it is never written, written only with its default, or a static written once with a constant in its own initialiser before that initialiser can run other code. javac has already folded `static final` compile-time constants: there is no branch left to find.

27 fields qualify in the whole build, and very few guard a branch. In `cli-noexp`, by what licensed the removal (outcomes, before capping at what JaCoCo counts on the line):

| fact | why | outcomes |
|---|---|---:|
| `tla2sany/semantic/LabelNode.subExpressionOf:Ltla2sany/semantic/SymbolNode;` | only ever written with its default | 1 |

| scope | branches, RTA | RTA+const | removed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `cli-noexp` | 10401 | 10400 | 1 |
| `port` | 9824 | 9824 | 0 |
| `cli` | 10776 | 10775 | 1 |
| `cli-nodebug` | 10380 | 10379 | 1 |
| `cli+xml-noexp` | 10773 | 10772 | 1 |
| `cli+xml` | 11148 | 11147 | 1 |
| `cli+xml-nodebug` | 10752 | 10751 | 1 |
| `parse-noexp` | 10328 | 10327 | 1 |
| `parse` | 10328 | 10327 | 1 |

The honest result: SANY barely has such branches, so sound reasoning at this level buys almost nothing. Removing more would need value tracking (what can this field hold at this point), which is where cheap and sound stop. The soundness check tests each fold against every run: a line whose instructions are all ruled out must not have run, and a line that lost an outcome cannot have hit more than the rest.

A cut also removes the guard outcome that leads into it: 1 handwritten outcome(s) in `cli-noexp`, `if (doDebugging)`'s true arm.

## Soundness

`staticreach check`, and every full run, compares each coverage report with its scope and exits 1 on anything unexplained: every method JaCoCo saw run must be reachable, at CHA, RTA and RTA+const. A spec run's harness is an extra root, recorded in the table; upstream's test classes are all roots, since JUnit calls them by reflection. Lines ruled out by a cut or a fold must not have run either, nor unreachable lexer arms, and every reflective site in reached code must be resolved.

**Result: 0 unexplained, 0 explained.**

## How the graph is built

A small class-file parser in `classfile.go` and `bytecode.go`; no text parsing of `javap`. Methods are name plus descriptor throughout.

- **Dispatch** follows JVMS 5.4.6 selection, so a call lands on a superclass's method or an interface default when that is what a class inherits.
- **JDK callbacks** come from the hierarchy, read from the JDK's jmods: a method is a callback when a JDK supertype of an instantiated class declares its exact signature and selection picks it. No list of names. `toString(int, Errors)` is not one.
- **Class initialisation** is modelled: `new`, `getstatic`, `putstatic`, `invokestatic`, plus superclasses and interfaces with default methods, per JVMS 5.5.
- **`invokedynamic`** reads the real bootstrap arguments. A lambda or method reference reaches its implementation method and instantiates a modelled class for its interface; string concatenation is a `toString()` on each argument type. Any other bootstrap stops the tool with an error.

`cli-noexp` under RTA reaches, by top package, in methods: `pcal` 509, `tla2sany` 1333, `tla2tex` 12, `tlc2` 14, `util` 115. Only `tla2sany` has JaCoCo counters; the rest are in `candidate-map.tsv` with blank branch columns.

## The lexer

The token manager has 3245 branches; specs hit 2587, the union 2591. Reachability of its automaton states is decidable and the state graph is easy to read from the generated source, so `lexer.go` does: every `jjMoveNfa_k` arm, every transition (`jjCheckNAdd*`, `jjAddStates`, direct `jjstateSet` writes, through `jjnextStates`), and every start (`jjMoveNfa_k(n, ...)`, `jjStartNfaWithStates_k`, the returns of `jjStopStringLiteralDfa_k`). This is about automaton arms only: grammar productions and choice points stay with the climb.

All six lexical states are reachable from `jjnewLexState` and `SwitchTo`.

| lexical state | NFA states | reached | arms | unreachable arms | branches on them | literal DFA bit tests | unsatisfiable |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DEFAULT | 12 | 12 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| PRAGMA | 58 | 50 | 69 | 8 | 22 | 0 | 0 |
| SPEC | 271 | 226 | 308 | 45 | 132 | 138 | 0 |
| IN_COMMENT | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| EMBEDDED | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| IN_EOL_COMMENT | 3 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

**54 arms cannot run, on any input:** no transition or start names their state. They hold 156 branches, of which the union hit 0. That is the check, and the tool fails if one ever runs. Most likely JavaCC merges these states' moves into composite start states and leaves their original arms with nothing to enter them; the generated code shows such merged arms, but this explanation was not checked against JavaCC's generator. The arms stay in the generated denominators above; subtracting them turns generated `cli-noexp` under RTA from 80.9% to 82.9% of 6353, specs, and is still a statement about the lexer alone.

By lexical state, input section and NFA state:

- PRAGMA: `curChar<64`: 12 (line 442), 23 (line 465); `64..127`: 13 (line 636), 20 (line 679), 21 (line 683), 22 (line 687), 39 (line 741), 50 (line 778);
- SPEC: `curChar<64`: 19 (line 3039), 32 (line 3051), 47 (line 3072), 106 (line 3112), 110 (line 3124), 127 (line 3157), 157 (line 3177), 161 (line 3189), 164 (line 3197), 221 (line 3316); `64..127`: 12 (line 3830), 17 (line 3842), 30 (line 3850), 39 (line 3866), 43 (line 3874), 51 (line 3882), 58 (line 3925), 59 (line 3929), 60 (line 3933), 61 (line 3937), 68 (line 3960), 84 (line 4024), 100 (line 4084), 133 (line 4120), 180 (line 4262), 191 (line 4295), 199 (line 4317), 244 (line 4415); `>=128`: 1 (line 4599), 20 (line 4603), 21 (line 4607), 22 (line 4611), 24 (line 4615), 25 (line 4619), 26 (line 4623), 27 (line 4627), 31 (line 4631), 40 (line 4639), 41 (line 4643), 44 (line 4647), 45 (line 4651), 48 (line 4655), 49 (line 4659), 50 (line 4663), 60 (line 4667);
- IN_EOL_COMMENT: `curChar<64`: 2 (line 872);

The literal DFA methods get a forward union of the active bit masks, in depth order: no bit test is unsatisfiable by the masks that reach it. That is a statement about the masks only.

What deciding the rest would take: the remaining missed branches sit inside reachable arms, on tests such as `kind > N` and the character masks, whose outcome depends on which NFA states are active together. Deciding those exactly means running the subset construction over the generated moves, active state sets against character classes, recording which outcome each test can take. It is finite and on the order of a few hundred lines that interpret the generated arms; it is not done here. `jjCanMove` above 127 would need the character tables too.

## Limits

- **Upper bound.** Reachable means not ruled out. A method in the map can be dead for reasons the graph cannot see, such as a check no value can fail. Unhit branches in the map are candidates, not known-reachable targets.
- **Whole methods.** Except for the fold and the cuts, every branch in a reachable method counts.
- **JDK as a black box.** JDK bodies are not analysed. Any override of a JDK-declared method on an instantiated class is assumed called; nothing checks that the object reaches that JDK call. This keeps it sound and keeps it loose.
- **Measuring that looseness.** 465 handwritten branches of `cli-noexp` (RTA) are reachable only through an assumed JDK callback, and specs hit 44 of them, so the assumption is doing real work and also inflating the denominator by an unknown part of the rest.
- **Classes no input provides.** 1 names looked up during the analysis are in neither the build nor the JDK, so nothing is inherited through them: `org/junit/runner/Runner`.
- **The test rows are weak.** Rooting all test methods reaches a lot; they mainly show the analysis does not drop reflection through the product. Spec runs are the bar.
- **Not run.** TLC was not started for this report. The `parse` scope follows `SpecProcessor.processSpec` from reading its source, so its seeds are by hand, and TLC's later use of the semantic graph is not an entry.
